Feeling GAN training through the forger-.src: Feeling GAN training through the forger-and-detective game

Forget the loss function for a moment. S.zh:
暂时忘掉损失函数。先从一名造假者与一名侦探说起，

Forget the loss function for a moment. S.src:
Forget the loss function for a moment. Start with a counterfeiter and a detective,
          give them paint and magnifying glasses, and watch a generative model emerge
          as a pencil-and-paper game—no black box, no hand-waving.

A counterfeiter prints fake banknotes. A.zh: 造假者印制假钞。侦探检查每一张经过银行的钞票。起初，造假者水平很差——假钞如同幼儿涂鸦，侦探一眼就能识破。侦探显得很聪明。造假者显得很可笑。
A counterfeiter prints fake banknotes. A.src: A counterfeiter prints fake banknotes. A detective inspects every bill that passes through a bank. At first, the counterfeiter is bad — the fakes look like kindergarten art, and the detective catches them instantly. The detective looks smart. The counterfeiter looks ridiculous.

But the counterfeiter learns. Every time.zh: 但造假者会学习。每当一张假钞被识破，她便问侦探：@@T0@@「你从哪里看出破绽的？」@@T1@@ 她修正那处缺陷。几百次迭代之后，假钞已能通过旧的检查——侦探必须找出新的破绽。几千次迭代之后，侦探的「检查」已细到分辨纸张纤维的毛糙。
But the counterfeiter learns. Every time.src: But the counterfeiter learns. Every time a fake is caught, she asks the detective: "What tipped you off?" She fixes that flaw. A few hundred iterations later the fakes pass muster on the old tests — the detective must find new ones. A few thousand iterations later the detective's "tests" are splitting hairs of the paper fiber.

At the limit, the counterfeiter's bills.zh: 在极限处，造假者的钞票与真钞已无法区分。侦探只能靠掷硬币。GAN 就是这场博弈，两名参与者是两个神经网络，而钞票是概率分布。
At the limit, the counterfeiter's bills.src: At the limit, the counterfeiter's bills are indistinguishable from real ones. The detective is left flipping coins. A GAN is this game, with two neural networks as the players and probability distributions as the bills.

@@T0@@Pause and think.@@T1@@ If you'd ne.src: Pause and think. If you'd never seen this density, how would you try to reproduce it? You could fit a parametric family (Gaussian mixture) — but what if the true shape isn't a mixture? A GAN skips that choice: the generator is a neural network, free to take any form. The training loss steers it toward pdata without ever assuming what shape it is.

Given a discriminator, the generator's j.src: Given a discriminator, the generator's job is to fool it. If D thinks real points have high score and fakes have low score, G wants to push its output toward regions where D is high.

@@T0@@Saturation warning.@@T1@@ If D is.zh: @@T0@@饱和警告。@@T1@@ 若 D 非常自信（对该样本输出 0.001），则 log D ≈ -6.9—一个巨大的负数，但梯度@@T2@@极小@@T3@@，因为对数导数 @@T4@@1/D@@T5@@ 变得不稳定。这正是 Goodfellow 的@@T6@@非饱和损失@@T7@@（最大化 log D 而非最小化 log(1-D)）所要解决的问题。
@@T0@@Saturation warning.@@T1@@ If D is.src: Saturation warning. If D is very confident (outputs 0.001 on this sample), log D ≈ -6.9 — a huge negative number but a tiny gradient because the log derivative 1/D becomes unstable. That's the vanishing-gradient problem Goodfellow's non-saturating loss (maximize log D instead of minimize log(1-D)) was designed to fix.

@@T0@@What the loss dynamics show.@@T1@@.zh: @@T0@@损失动态说明了什么。@@T1@@ 两个损失是@@T2@@振荡@@T3@@的，而非单调下降。这是@@T4@@意料之中@@T5@@的—当 G 改进时，D 的任务变难；当 D 调整时，G 的梯度随之改变。这种振荡就是共舞。在收敛时，两个损失都稳定在一个不动点附近（对类 DPPM 的极小极大目标而言约为 log 4 ≈ 1.38）。
@@T0@@What the loss dynamics show.@@T1@@.src: What the loss dynamics show. The two losses oscillate, not monotonically decrease. This is expected — when G improves, D's job gets harder; when D adjusts, G's gradient shifts. The oscillation is the dance. At convergence both losses settle around a fixed point (log 4 ≈ 1.38 for the DPPM-like minimax objective).

Mode collapse · when the dance breaks do.zh: 模式崩塌 · 当共舞瓦解时
Mode collapse · when the dance breaks do.src: Mode collapse · when the dance breaks down

In the ideal trajectory above, G learns.zh: 在上述理想轨迹中，G 学到了完整的分布。实践中，G 常常走捷径：它发现某一个特定的输出能很好地骗过 D，于是对每个输入都只产生@@T0@@那一个输出@@T1@@。多样性丧失—这便是@@T2@@模式崩塌@@T3@@。
In the ideal trajectory above, G learns.src: In the ideal trajectory above, G learns the full distribution. In practice, G often takes a shortcut: it discovers that one particular output fools D well, and produces only that output for every input. Diversity is lost — mode collapse.

@@T0@@Mode-collapse demonstration@@T1@@..zh: @@T0@@模式崩塌演示@@T1@@。切换情景，观察生成器如何在训练推进的过程中仍执拗于双峰目标中的单一个众峰。
@@T0@@Mode-collapse demonstration@@T1@@..src: Mode-collapse demonstration. Toggle the scenario and watch the generator fixate on just one mode of a bimodal target, even as training proceeds.

@@T0@@Why collapse happens.@@T1@@ If G's.zh: @@T0@@崩塌为何发生。@@T1@@ 若 G 在某点的输出以 0.49 的置信度骗过 D，梯度信号便很弱。若另一点也以 0.49 的置信度骗过 D，G 就没有理由同时产生两者—它会收敛到更容易的那一个。防止崩塌需要额外的技巧：小批量判别、WGAN 的推土机距离、谱归一化，或仅仅是用心地调参。
@@T0@@Why collapse happens.@@T1@@ If G's.src: Why collapse happens. If G's output at some point fools D with confidence 0.49, the gradient signal is weak. If another point fools D with confidence 0.49 too, G has no reason to produce both — it converges on the easier one. Preventing collapse needs extra tricks: minibatch discrimination, WGAN's earth-mover distance, spectral normalization, or just careful hyperparameter tuning.

@@T0@@\"GANs minimize a meaningful loss..zh:
@@T0@@「GAN 最小化一个有意义的损失。」@@T1@@@@T2@@
              @@T3@@极小极大@@T4@@目标并不允许一种单一的「损失下降」解读。D 的损失上升可能意味着 G 变好了；G 的损失上升可能意味着 D 识破了。仅凭监控损失来判断 GAN 的进展是非常糟糕的做法—应使用样本质量与多样性指标（FID、精确率/召回率）。
@@T0@@\"GANs minimize a meaningful loss..src:
"GANs minimize a meaningful loss."
The minimax objective doesn't admit a single "loss goes down" interpretation. D's loss going up might mean G got better; G's loss going up might mean D caught on. Monitoring losses alone is a terrible way to judge GAN progress — use sample quality + diversity metrics (FID, precision/recall).

@@T0@@\"The generator learns p@@T1@@data.zh:
@@T0@@「生成器学到了 p@@T1@@data@@T2@@。」@@T3@@@@T4@@
              只是近似地学到，且仅在理想化的纳什均衡处。实践中，G 常常只学到 p@@T7@@data@@T8@@ 的一个看起来不错的@@T5@@子集@@T6@@。这正是 WGAN、Wasserstein 距离与正则化方法重要的原因—它们把模型推向更完整的分布。
@@T0@@\"The generator learns p@@T1@@data.src:
"The generator learns pdata."
Only approximately, and only at the idealised Nash equilibrium. In practice, G often learns a good-looking subset of pdata. This is why WGAN, Wasserstein distance, and regularisers matter — they push the model closer to the full distribution.

@@T0@@\"You should train D to convergenc.zh:
@@T0@@「在更新 G 之前应把 D 训练到收敛。」@@T1@@@@T2@@
              原论文曾如此建议；但实践中这会扼杀 G 的梯度（D 越强，越饱和，G 的梯度就越小）。多数 GAN 配方交替各走一步，或使用非饱和的 G 损失以保持稳健。
@@T0@@\"You should train D to convergenc.src:
"You should train D to convergence before updating G."
The original paper suggested this; in practice it kills G's gradient (the stronger D gets, the more it saturates, the smaller G's gradient). Most GAN recipes alternate one step of each, or use the non-saturating G loss to stay robust.

From minimax to Wasserstein · why traini.zh: 从极小极大到 Wasserstein · 训练为何变得更容易
From minimax to Wasserstein · why traini.src: From minimax to Wasserstein · why training got easier

The original GAN objective measures a Je.zh: 原始 GAN 目标衡量的是 p@@T0@@data@@T1@@ 与 p@@T2@@G@@T3@@ 之间的 Jensen-Shannon 散度。问题在于：JS 会饱和—当两个分布几乎不重叠时（训练初期），无论它们相距多近或多远，JS ≈ log 2。因此生成器得不到有用的梯度信号。
The original GAN objective measures a Je.src: The original GAN objective measures a Jensen-Shannon divergence between p<sub>data</sub> and p<sub>G</sub>. The problem: JS is saturating — when the distributions barely overlap (early in training), JS ≈ log 2 no matter how close or far they are. So the generator gets no useful gradient signal.

Arjovsky et al. 2017 (WGAN) replaced JS.zh: Arjovsky 等人于 2017 年（WGAN）用 @@T0@@Wasserstein-1（推土机）距离@@T1@@ 取代了 JS：
Arjovsky et al. 2017 (WGAN) replaced JS.src: Arjovsky et al. 2017 (WGAN) replaced JS with the Wasserstein-1 (earth-mover) distance:

Think of it as \"the minimum cost to phy.zh: 可以把它想成「把 p@@T0@@G@@T1@@ 的质量实际搬运到 p@@T2@@data@@T3@@ 上的最小代价」。随着分布彼此靠近，该距离@@T4@@连续地@@T5@@缩小—不会饱和。训练因而稳定得多。
Think of it as \"the minimum cost to phy.src: Think of it as "the minimum cost to physically move the mass of pG onto pdata." This distance shrinks continuously as the distributions get closer — no saturation. Training is dramatically more stable.

Gradient when distributions far apart.zh: 分布相距较远时的梯度

Healthy when G is bad.zh: 当 G 较差时仍然健康

Healthy always (linear in distance).zh: 始终健康（随距离线性变化）

@@T0@@Connection to diffusion (L21-L22)..zh: @@T0@@与扩散模型的联系（L21-L22）。@@T1@@ 扩散模型完全避开了 GAN 的难题，因为它从不要求两个分布同时匹配。它教单个模型一步步消除噪声，使用回归损失（对预测噪声的均方误差）—没有对抗博弈，没有模式崩塌，没有极小极大。这正是扩散模型在 2022-23 年于多数实用图像生成任务中取代 GAN 的主要原因。
@@T0@@Connection to diffusion (L21-L22)..src: Connection to diffusion (L21-L22). Diffusion models avoid the GAN problem entirely by never asking two distributions to match at once. They teach a single model to undo noise step by step, with a regression loss (MSE on predicted noise) — no adversarial game, no mode collapse, no minimax. That's the main reason diffusion displaced GANs for most practical image generation in 2022-23.

@@T0@@Final takeaway.@@T1@@ When someone.zh: @@T0@@最终要点。@@T1@@ 当有人说「GAN 训练不稳定」时，他们描述的正是你刚才驱动的那些动态。生成器与判别器在一个 10⁹ 维空间中彼此追逐，绕着鞍点打转—它居然能工作本身就是一个奇迹。WGAN、谱归一化以及大规模工程（StyleGAN、BigGAN）使其@@T2@@可靠地@@T3@@工作，并非因为他们发现了新思想，而是因为他们驯服了上述的共舞。
@@T0@@Final takeaway.@@T1@@ When someone.src: Final takeaway. When someone says "GAN training is unstable," they're describing the exact dynamics you just drove. The generator and discriminator are chasing each other around a saddle point in a 10⁹-dimensional space — the miracle is that it works at all. WGAN, spectral norm, and large-scale engineering (StyleGAN, BigGAN) made it work reliably, not because they found a new idea but because they tamed the dance above.
